scope_allowed: Relevance of the quantities of interest

models.name: Model A: Anatomy-resolved explicit FE
models.what_it_computes: Time-resolved insertion force versus depth using a 3D subject-specific cochlear geometry with nonlinear contact, rate-dependent viscoelastic soft tissues, and Coulomb friction between electrode and cochlear walls.

models.name: Model B: Simplified explicit FE beam-in-shell
models.what_it_computes: Peak insertion force envelope and force–depth slope using a curvature-matched parametric cochlear shell and a beam representation of the electrode with aggregated contact/friction laws.

mechanisms.name: Lateral-wall frictional drag
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sustained friction against the lateral wall dominates steady insertion force and correlates with risk of epithelial microtrauma.

mechanisms.name: Modiolus-side binding
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Intermittent contact with the modiolus produces transient force spikes that can precipitate tip deflection and inner-wall trauma.

mechanisms.name: Tip fold-over initiation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Onset of tip fold-over dramatically increases force and is linked to insertion failure and postoperative map instability.

mechanisms.name: Sheath/bucker sleeve buckling
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Local instability of guiding sleeves raises insertion force and can transfer load to delicate intracochlear structures.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–7 Credibility Index per (model × mechanism) pair, with 0 = no evidence and 7 = compelling evidence.

expected_decision.outcome_source: Under the stated Context of Use—preoperative planning for electrode type and strategy selection—Model A supports mechanism-aware guidance for friction-dominated force behavior and hazard-flagging for modiolus binding and fold-over, with moderate confidence for sleeve buckling.

datasets: 24 subject-specific cochlear geometries from clinical CT
18 transparent scala-tympani phantom insertions with force–depth traces at 0.5–2.0 mm/s
20 fresh-frozen cadaveric insertions with synchronized endoscopic labeling of binding events
18 cadaveric preparations to evaluate tip fold-over onset with micro-CT confirmation
acceptance_criteria: when a predicted basal force plateau exceeds 60 mN for a given subject at 1.0 mm/s insertion speed, the plan may shift to a more lubricious regimen or slower advancement
Predicted transient spikes above 100 mN or early-onset fold-over risk may lead to a change in electrode variant with reduced stiffness or altered tip geometry
time-to-result targets are set to less than 3 hours for the detailed model and less than 10 minutes for the simplified model
predefined acceptance bands for peak and slope changes (<3% and <5%, respectively)

name_keywords: TPR 0.78, FPR 0.19; timing offset 0.9 mm; amplitude error 11 mN
14/18 correctly classified; onset median error 1.3 mm; surge error 15 mN
7/18 correctly classified; onset error 3.7 mm; surge underestimation 45%
critical loads within 8% and post-buckling slopes within 12%
estimated thresholds deviated by 35% on average
